problem.text: The manifest explicitly included only Hadamard data, while the JIT loader needs native source files beneath the installed exllamav3 package.

reasoning.text: Explicitly including the extension tree addresses the source-availability requirement of deferred compilation without requiring installation-time precompilation.

impact.text: The change adds recursive inclusion of the entire extension directory, preserves Hadamard-data inclusion, and leaves compiler configuration and runtime loading unchanged.

limitations: No distribution build, installation, or JIT compilation was executed; actual archive and wheel contents remain unverified.
A scalar computation would not validate this packaging change; its meaningful check requires building and inspecting installation artifacts.

chapters.title: Ship native sources for deferred compilation

claims.text: MANIFEST.in adds `recursive-include exllamav3/exllamav3_ext *`. Unlike a compilation-unit-only filter, this requests the whole nested extension tree, allowing supporting files as well as native compilation units to accompany the package.

setup.py enables include_package_data and disables precompilation whenever EXLLAMA_NOCOMPILE is present, regardless of its value. With precompilation enabled and Torch available, it instead supplies CUDAExtension and BuildExtension to setuptools.

At runtime, ext.py first imports exllamav3_ext. On ModuleNotFoundError it walks the extension directory relative to its own installed file, collects .c, .cpp and .cu files, and passes them to torch.utils.cpp_extension.load together with that directory as an include path. The manifest addition supports this existing fallback rather than changing how compilation is selected.
The earlier installation entry documents both precompiled and EXLLAMA_NOCOMPILE installation paths and notes the original manifest's Hadamard-data inclusion.

annotation.summary: Explicitly includes the native extension tree in the package manifest to support the existing JIT-compilation fallback.
